methods.name: VQ-V AE decoders
methods.description: Used for fast upsampling of top level tokens to hear a rough sense of generated content.

methods.name: Human-in-the-loop co-composition process
methods.description: Involves generating multiple samples, human selection of a favorite sample, and continuation of generation based on the selected sample.

methods.name: Distillation
methods.description: Process of transferring information from a model with slow autoregressive sampling but fast parallel likelihood evaluation to a model with fast parallel sampling but slow autoregressive likelihood evaluation.

methods.name: raw audio hierarchical VQ-V AE
methods.description: A model trained for twice as long as previous models, but middle and top-level reconstructions were not capturing much information.

methods.name: ancestral_sampling
methods.description: used to explore different possibilities by generating multiple continuations from the same segment.

methods.name: Parallel WaveNet
methods.description: Improves upon WaveNet by using a mixture of logistics distribution and performing probability density distillation to learn a parallel feed-forward network from a pre-trained autoregressive model.

methods.name: ClariNet
methods.description: Achieves similar audio quality to Parallel WaveNet using a simple Gaussian distribution and a closed-form loss function, eliminating the need for Monte-Carlo sampling.

methods.name: SampleRNN
methods.description: Uses a multi-scale, hierarchical recurrent neural network with convolutional upsampling to model long-range complex structures.

methods.name: WaveRNN
methods.description: Uses recurrent neural networks that operate separately on the most significant and the least significant bytes, allowing efficient deployment in mobile devices.

methods.name: WaveGlow
methods.description: A flow-based model for parallel sample-level audio synthesis, trained with a straightforward maximum-likelihood estimation.

methods.name: nonautoregressive decoders
methods.description: Decoders that do not rely on sequential processing
